elicitation_input.question: Which planet has a 'great red spot'?

llm_generation.text:
Jupiter has the famous "Great Red Spot" — a massive storm system that has been raging in its atmosphere for at least 350 years, possibly longer. 

Some key facts about it:

- It's an enormous anticyclonic storm, larger than Earth (though it has been shrinking in recent decades)
- Winds within the storm can reach speeds of up to 400 mph (640 km/h)
- Its reddish color is thought to result from chemical compounds brought up from lower in Jupiter's atmosphere that react with sunlight, though the exact composition is still debated
- It was first observed by astronomers in the 17th century, possibly by Giovanni Cassini or Robert Hooke, though continuous observation records date back to the 1830s

The storm has been monitored closely by telescopes and spacecraft, and while it has decreased in size over the past century, it remains one of the most striking features of our solar system.
